periodFactors._note: ASSUMPTION: hourly volume relative to the PM peak hour on arterials; typical urban weekday profile, to be calibrated.

kFactorNote: ASSUMPTION: peak-hour share of ADT for urban arterials (typically 0.08-0.10); not derived from local data.

classDefaultAdt._note: ASSUMPTION: per-class default two-way ADT when no count exists for the gate street. Documented values; a class with at least classDefaultFromCounts.minStreets counted streets takes their median instead (DATA-derived, see the build log); uncalibrated otherwise.

classDefaultFromCounts._decision: Switched off on 2026-11-12 (minStreets set out of reach). Counted streets are the busiest of their class, so their median overstates uncounted gates: it raised tertiary from 5,000 to 12,200 ADT and made the baseline less stable (150 vs 88 vehicles removed per PM hour).
classDefaultFromCounts._note: DATA: the default ADT of a gate class is the median ADT of the counted streets of that class in this data set (a TMC leg's peak-hour entering plus leaving volume over K, or a Caltrans station ADT times its factor; one value per street) when at least `minStreets` such streets exist; otherwise the documented value above stays. Counted streets are the busiest of their class, so the median is a high estimate for the uncounted gates.

streetCounts._note: DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour turning-movement counts at Telegraph Ave & Alcatraz Ave (Quality Counts; 2018-09-11, 2018-09-12, 2019-09-10, 2021-09-29), averaged. Leg volumes entering/leaving the intersection are used for gates lying on that leg's street in that compass direction from the count intersection (N/E/S/W). A gate takes the leg of the nearest counted intersection on its street and compass direction (within maxLegDistM), so gates far from this intersection use it as a proxy.

DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour turning-movement counts at Telegraph Ave & 40th St (Quality Counts; 2018-09-11, 2018-09-12, 2019-09-10, 2021-09-29), averaged. Intersection lies ~90 m south of the model edge; the north leg serves the Telegraph Ave gate on the south edge.
DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour counts at West St & 40th St (same four count dates), averaged. Serves the West St and 40th St gates on the south edge.
DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour counts at Market St & 55th St (same four count dates), averaged. Serves the Market St and 55th St gates.

adtOverrides.source: SR-13 at Claremont Ave, Berkeley PM 10.79, ahead AADT 23,500 (back 32,500): the ahead side of SR-13 is Ashby Ave west of Claremont Ave, so the station sits on that block, 65 m west of the junction (Caltrans 2023-24 count year). Until the sixteenth round this record was applied to Claremont Ave with a factor of 0.6.
SR-13 Ashby Ave at the SR-123 junction (San Pablo Ave), Berkeley PM 13.178, back AADT 28,000 (east side; ahead 43,500): applies to the Ashby Ave gate at the west edge (Caltrans 2023-24 count year).
SR-13 at Domingo Ave, Berkeley PM 10.69, back AADT 27,000 (east side; ahead 32,500): applies to the Tunnel Road gate east of the SR-24/SR-13 ramps (Caltrans 2023-24 count year).
SR-123 San Pablo Ave at JCT RTE 13, Berkeley PM 1.906, back AADT 21,700 (ahead 22,800).
SR-123 San Pablo Ave at Stanford Ave, Oakland PM 1.12, AADT 21,300 back / 19,700 ahead (mean 20,500).

streetMatch._note: Lower-case substrings of OSM link names mapped to a count key.

gravity.balanceNote: Through-trip balancing: counted gates keep their outflow target and the assumed gates are scaled to the inflow supply (before, every gate was scaled to 0.77 of its target).

local._note: ASSUMPTION: vehicle trip rates per resident worker / per job per weekday; ITE-like order of magnitude, uncalibrated.
local.vehicleModeShareNote: ASSUMPTION: drive-alone+carpool share for commutes (ACS-like; not derived here).
local.sideRuleNote: ASSUMPTION (round 19): a census block loads only nodes on its own side of the study-area boundary (polygon or boundary street counts as inside; a block is inside when its centroid is in the polygon). Before, blocks across a boundary street loaded the boundary corners, which are study-area nodes, so cars bound for places across Alcatraz Ave and Telegraph Ave ended at the corner and were not through cars.
local.spreadRadiusNote: ASSUMPTION: a census block loads every node on a residential street within this distance of its centroid, in equal parts (the nearest node when none is that close). Before the seventeenth round each block loaded only its nearest node, which put the trips of several blocks on one corner.

countCalibration.neighborNote: ASSUMPTION (round 20): census blocks whose loading node lies outside the study area but within 250 m of it are the same neighborhood across the boundary street, and the assumed trip rate misses the same non-work trips there, so they take the study area's factor times neighborScale. The side rule of round 19 moved the trips of these blocks off the boundary corners, which are study-area nodes, and left them at the unscaled rate: cars entering Colby St, Hillegass Ave and Dana St from Alcatraz Ave fell from 325 to 136 veh/h against 360 counted. Tested 400 m x 1.0 (PM removals 3.0 per hour), 400 m x 0.5 (1.2) and 250 m x 1.0 (0.0).
countCalibration._note: DATA-derived multiplier on the trip rates of blocks inside the study area: the external trip ends they offer are scaled to the ends the volunteer count implies (vehicles entering less the whole-street through cars; vehicles leaving less the same). The per-resident-worker rate above counts workers only (LODES resident workers), so it misses residents who do not work and non-work trips. Midday has no count: the mean of the AM and PM factors (ASSUMPTION). maxScale is a sanity cap (ASSUMPTION).
countCalibration.maxScaleNote: ASSUMPTION: raised from 4 to 8 in round 19. With the side rule the study area's own blocks offer 174 and 132 external trip ends at the assumed rate and the count implies about 800, so the factors are 4.6 and 6.2.

freewayNote: Links of these classes form the freeway. Gates on them are freeway gates: they only exchange trips with surface streets through the ramps found in the network (surface nodes touched by both freeway and surface links). Freeway mainline-to-mainline trips are not generated (they never touch surface streets).

ramps._note: Ramp demand. DATA: ramp ADT rows from Caltrans ramp-volume workbooks (raw.caltransRamps), matched to network ramps by street name (streetMatch) and type (OFF TO / ON FR); latest count year used, no growth applied (ASSUMPTION). Everything below is ASSUMPTION unless stated.
ramps.kFactorNote: ASSUMPTION: peak-hour share of ramp ADT, same urban range as the arterial K-factor; period volume factors (periodFactors) apply on top.
ramps.defaultAdtNote: ASSUMPTION: ADT of a ramp with no matching published count (minor connectors at the SR-13/SR-24 interchange, hillside ramps and the Broadway terminals east of Tunnel Road). The original four ramps never used it.
ramps.localShareNote: ASSUMPTION (calibration step V: 0.30 -> 0.60, tested 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.60 / 0.75): share of ramp trips whose surface end is an in-area (LODES) node rather than a surface gate. The model area is 5.7 by 3.4 km, so most ramp trips end inside it. These trips replace part of the block's external local trips.
ramps.maxShareOfGateNote: ASSUMPTION: ramp trips use at most this share of a surface gate's in/outflow target (surface totals stay consistent; the Furness step fills the rest).

choice._note: ASSUMPTION (round 25): ramp choice made upstream. The simulator picks the off-ramp of a trip from the mainline gate by its own costs, and the two Claremont Ave ramps differ by seconds for most destinations, so the split between them followed noise and queues (52nd St 900, Clifton St 883 against 1,024 and 617 counted). The count fit already divides each off-ramp flow over the ramps its final assignment uses, and that assignment meets the ramp counts and the counts downstream of each terminal. The builder splits each off-ramp flow by those shares and writes the ramp as the flow's `via`. maxDetour: the simulator keeps the ramp while its route costs at most this multiple of the plain route, else it tries the flow's other ramps, then the plain route (as for assumed movements). minShare: a ramp that carries less of a flow is dropped and its trips go to the others.

destination._note: ASSUMPTION: gravity over surface gates and local nodes, attraction x direction plausibility. Plausibility = exp(-(dTheta/sigma)^2) floored, where dTheta is the angle between the bearing ramp->destination and the bearing ramp->study-area center. No distance term. Street choice is left to the simulator.
destination.poolingNote: Surface ends of ramp trips are drawn per ramp ('ramp') instead of once per mainline gate over every ramp the gate reaches ('gate'): ramps far apart that feed one gate (Claremont/Hudson and Miles on the WB gate, the Caldecott and Broadway Terrace ramps) were pooled, so trips from the whole west side were sent to the Claremont on-ramp. Each ramp keeps its own DATA volume, bearing and access time. Round nine: the importer now merges the freeway-edge stubs (one mainline gate per direction and end), which removes the reason the pools were first made, but the merged gate reaches every ramp of its direction (9 or 10, up to 4.5 km apart), so a gate pool would again mix distant ramps; per-ramp pools stay (PM, seeds 1 to 3, simulator: removals 0 / 0 / 0 against 1 / 2 / 0 with gate pools).
destination.accessTauS_note: ASSUMPTION: access decay of a ramp trip's surface end, exp(-t / accessTauS) with t the router's generalized cost in seconds from the surface end to the ramp (to it for an on-ramp, from it for an off-ramp). 150, 300 and 600 s were tried (baseline-calibration record, eighth round); 0 turns it off.

ramps.aliasNote: ASSUMPTION: the Caltrans descriptions (EB OFF TO BROADWAY, WB OFF TO COLLEGE AVE, ...) are matched to ramp terminals by location, from OSM destination tags and postmile order, because the surface street names at the terminals (Keith Ave, Miles Ave, Brookside Ave, Broadway) differ. Verify against Caltrans ramp maps before relying on them.
ramps.excludeNote: Rows that combine the 52nd St and MLK Jr Way (Grove St) ramps are dropped because per-street SEG rows (2016-2017 / 2012) exist for the same ramps and would double count.
ramps.studyEndFreewayCapNote: Optional (round 19, not set): at most this share of a study-area block's external trip ends pairs with a freeway. Tried at 0.5 and 0.7: headline shares fell to 30 to 53 points (below observed) and through cars fell, so it is off.

active._note: ASSUMPTION unless stated: walking and biking demand (design D6). Person trips use the car model's per-worker and per-job rates (local.*), then these mode shares. Volumes are persons per hour. Only the count scaling below uses data (DATA: Oakland pedestrian and bicycle counts at one intersection); everything else is uncounted. ACS commute mode shares were not retrievable (the Census API needs a key), so the shares are not derived from them.

pedestrian.modeShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of person trips made on foot; the observed count scaling overrides the absolute level.
pedestrian.meanTripNote: ASSUMPTION: mean of the exponential trip-length decay (network meters).
pedestrian.maxTripNote: ASSUMPTION: longest walk to another in-area node.
pedestrian.commercialShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of in-area walking trips ending on a primary or secondary street inside the study area (shops, services).
pedestrian.gateShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of walking trips leaving or entering the model at a gate.
pedestrian.gateMaxNote: ASSUMPTION: gates beyond this network distance get no walking trips.
pedestrian.periodVolumeNote: ASSUMPTION: hourly volume relative to the PM peak (the scaling period).

bicycle.modeShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of person trips made by bicycle; the observed count scaling overrides the absolute level.
bicycle.meanTripNote: ASSUMPTION: mean of the exponential trip-length decay (network meters).
bicycle.gateShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of cycling trips leaving or entering the model at a gate.
bicycle.throughNote: ASSUMPTION: gate-to-gate bicycle trips as a share of all trips starting at in-area nodes.
bicycle.routeBonusNote: ASSUMPTION: gate pairs whose shortest bike path runs along bike lanes and routes get up to 1 + routeBonus times the weight.
bicycle.laneRouteCostNote: ASSUMPTION: bike-path cost of a link with a bike lane (routes use the midpoint to 1); only steers which shortest path counts as the cyclist's.
bicycle.periodVolumeNote: ASSUMPTION: hourly volume relative to the PM peak (the scaling period).

countScaling._note: The factors fit PM counts at streetCounts[0]. The pedestrian target counts planned crosswalk traversals on the simulator's sidewalk routes. The bicycle target counts routes passing the intersection, including trip ends. The final flow list is checked after the cap. Each factor applies across all periods and places.

active.maxFlowsNote: Keeps all modes together under about 12,000 flows per period (cars are capped at maxFlows above, 8,000).

peripheral._note: ASSUMPTION: gate-to-gate trips that never come within nearM of the study area are kept as background load. P1: pairs whose gates are less than minPerimeterGapM apart along the model-area perimeter, or whose free-flow route stays within edgeBandM of the model edge, are corner-clipping and are not generated (their volume goes to other pairs at the same gates, so counted gates keep their counts). P2: a gate's modeled volume may not exceed min(its target, its lane capacity x cordon.signalizedVehPerHourPerLane); the excess is taken from that gate's peripheral through trips only. Ramp volumes and counted volumes are never reduced.

cordon._note: Measured capacities of the validation suite (data/calibration/validation.md): a signalized lane at green share 0.5 (cases b1, b2) and a motorway lane at 65 mph (case i1).

recency._note: ASSUMPTION (round 24, project lead decision of 2026-11-14: the newer data is more important than the 2010 and 2013 data). Every station carries the count year of its source (derived from the file names, count dates and release years in the provenance; a source without a known year is treated as old). A station's weight is multiplied by the weight of the first band whose maxAgeYears is at least its age (reference year minus count year); a weight of 0 takes the station out of the fit and scores it as held out. The 10-year edge and the old-band weight are not from a study: they separate the 2010 and 2013 environmental-review counts and the 2012 ramp counts (age 13 to 16) from the 2018 to 2025 sources (age 1 to 8) and were tested at 1, 0.5, 0.25 and 0 (data/calibration/rockridge.record.md, twenty-fourth round). recentYears only sets what the reports call recent.
recency.exemptRampsNote: ASSUMPTION (round 25): freeway ramp counts keep full weight whatever their age. The two Claremont Ave off-ramps have no count newer than 2010 and 2013 (52nd St 1,024, Clifton St 617) and the Caltrans rows of the Telegraph Ave and Claremont Ave ramps are of 2012, so they are the only evidence of the ramp split. Down-weighted to 0.5 the static fit put 1,045 and 752 on the two ramps; at full weight it puts 1,015 and 631.
recency.growthNote: No growth from the count year: the published counts held (Caltrans SR-24 ramp ADT 2012 to 2019 and 2024; OakDOT counts at Telegraph Ave and Alcatraz Ave 2018 to 2021) are flat or lower, so there is no verified rate to apply. The key maps a source id (oakland-tmc, caltrans-aadt, caltrans-ramp, volunteer-count, CHRCO-EIR2014, SafewayCollege-DEIR2011) to an annual rate; empty means none.

countFit._note: Count-constrained demand (seventh round). Every count the pipeline holds is a target volume on directed links; OD flows are scaled so that a free-flow static assignment matches them. Citation for the method family: [VanZuylen1980], [Willumsen1981]. Targets for AM and midday are the PM counts scaled by periodFactors (ASSUMPTION).

bounds._note: ASSUMPTION: limits on a flow's cumulative factor. The matrix-estimation methods the fit follows ([VanZuylen1980], [Willumsen1981]) set no limit; the limits keep one count from rewriting a flow. Ramp flows go to 10 since the seventh round. Local flows go to 10 since the seventeenth: their prior comes from trip rates per resident worker that miss non-work trips, and inside the study area the volunteer count put the trip ends at 3.4 to 4.2 times that prior, above the old limit of 3.

countFit.drawsNote: ASSUMPTION: each flow is split equally over this many draws of perceived free-flow costs (probit loading [Sheffi1985] ch. 11.2: each link and movement cost normal with variance `dispersion` x the cost, the simulator's `ROUTE_DISPERSION_S`); 1 draw and dispersion 0 gives all-or-nothing assignment.

uncounted._note: ASSUMPTION: a flow that passes no counted link takes the volume-weighted median factor of the counted flows of its type (through, local, ramp); alternatives: medianAll, one.

weights._note: Weights of the constraint families in the geometric mean over the counted links of a flow's paths.

capacityGuard._note: ASSUMPTION-labeled sanity guard, not data: an uncounted link may carry at most capacity x (1 + excessShare); flows above are scaled down proportionally. Capacities are the simulator's own measured values from data/calibration/validation.md (cases named in each entry), per lane or per approach by the control at the link's end node. Counted links are exempt.

two_way_stop_minor.source: validation e4 (minor through, major 200 per direction)

two_way_stop_major.source: validation g1 (free single lane at 25 mph)

motorway_signal.source: validation i2 (off-ramp terminal at a signal)

countFit.convergenceNote: Stopping rule of the fit: every count station outside tolerance is either blocked (the flows it needs to move sit on a bound, share >= blockedShare) or in tension (another station outside tolerance the other way shares at least half of its flow, or the capacity guard pulls most of its flow down), and the volume-weighted mean relative step of the flows is below softStep; otherwise stop as stalled (worst log error of the other stations improved by less than stallGain over stallWindow iterations), or when no flow moves by more than `stationary`. Blocked and tense stations are listed in the fit report with what holds them back.

measured._note: Outer loop (tools/cost-loop.ts): mean delay per vehicle on each link from a simulator run (seed 1) is added to the free-flow cost of the static assignment; the BPR factor is switched off (alpha 0) because the measured delay already contains the congestion. ASSUMPTION: the control delay the router adds at the link end is subtracted so queues at signals count once. The file is optional: without it, or for another network, the assignment uses free-flow and BPR costs.

assignment._note: method 'free': the free-flow assignment over `draws` draws of perceived costs (draws and dispersion above). Method 'msa': stochastic capacity-restrained assignment: each pass loads every flow on `drawsPerPass` draws of perceived costs (probit loading [DaganzoSheffi1977] [Sheffi1985] ch. 11.2, the simulator's route choice: each link and movement cost normal with variance `dispersion` x the cost, shortest path on the draw) over link costs x BPR(volume / capacity), volumes averaged over passes (method of successive averages [PowellSheffi1982]); BPR form [Spiess1990] with alpha 0.15 and beta 4 (ASSUMPTION: the usual values); capacities from capacityGuard.capacity; `rounds` > 1 refits the table and reassigns at its own volumes.

shares._note: Observed route shares (StreetLight select-link and ramp via-street shares) as ratio constraints in the same fit, weight below the counts' (1 to 2) because the shares come from a device sample (ASSUMPTION: 0.5). 0 or enabled false leaves them out.
shares._weightNote: Round 19: 0.5 -> 3. At 1.5 and 3 the static route shares met their targets within 10 points; the extra weight changed little beyond 1.5 and PM removals held at 0.30 per hour at 3.

validation._note: Hold-out of count stations (design D17, [WebTAG-M3.1] C.3.2 and 4.2.1; audit C2; change protect-calibration-evidence). Stations that share a source observation form one dependency group. Within each corridor (the street of a gate, the intersection of a turning-movement count, the street of a Caltrans station, all freeway ramps together) the groups are ordered by a hash of their id and every fourth is held, never fewer than one per corridor; no count value is read. The split is frozen in splitFile (npm run data:split) before any count-derived step. The build runs twice: the shipped view fits all counts, the training view (--view training) removes the held groups' observations from gate totals, ramp volumes, trip ends, assumed movements and the fit, and its demand goes to demandOutput for a simulator run.

implied._note: DERIVED volumes on the select-link blocks: ramp count x via-street share / freeway share of the street's traffic (tools/lib/share-targets.ts impliedVolumes). Soft constraint with the share weight, below the counts.

gatePriorTotals._note: Calibration round 50, scope changed in round 52. In a period whose stations take simulated membership, the fit first runs as the baseline does (static membership, no ceilings); every gate direction and every non-gate node direction OUTSIDE the study area (the network's inStudyArea flag) that no gate station in the fit counts is then held, by a one-sided soft constraint of the given weight, to at most its car total in that static fit times (1 + tolerancePct / 100), and a hard projection guarantees it on the final flows (tools/lib/demand-fit.ts gatePriorStations, projectToCeilings). Non-gate nodes inside the study area have no ceiling, so the fit may add trip ends along the counted streets (round 51's fit could not, and the counted whole-street traversals want trips that begin or end along the street). Round 49's growth was entirely outside the study area, which this scope still caps. A regularizer toward the static fit: tolerancePct 0 and weight 10 (five times the ramp weight) are ASSUMPTIONS, not sourced. No count value sets a ceiling. The loop's 3% abort above the static fit bounds total volume. Periods without simulated membership (the loop's pass 0, midday) have no ceilings and no second fit.

simulatedMembership._note: Calibration round 48, extended in rounds 51 and 52. Every fitted station the report binary exports (link stations with a detector list or counted at the block, movement and route stations) takes its membership from simulated trips: each pair's share of trips at the station over seed runs of the demand of the same view, pooled with equal weight over the loop's passes (tools/membership-loop.ts), with the static share as a prior worth priorTrips trips (ASSUMPTION). Stations without an export (gate totals) and periods without runs (midday) keep static membership. The training view reads trainingFile, built only from runs of the cross-validation demand and naming no withheld station. The files are under target/ and are not committed. Round 51 sub-switches, both absent in rounds 48 to 50: throughTargets takes the through-car targets (select-link blocks marked fitThrough) and shares takes the select-link share constraints from the runs' block export (calibrate --select-od, blocks): the pairs of every trip that used a link of the block, pooled like the stations. A share's denominator membership of a pair is its simulated share of trips on the block with the static fraction as a prior worth priorTrips trips (ASSUMPTION); its numerator is the same for pairs whose origin (from) or destination (to) is a freeway node and 0 for the rest. A block without a simulated trip keeps static routes and is listed. Ramp via-street shares keep static routes: nothing exports them per pair. While this entry is present it replaces the hand-picked measuredStations list and the measured file. Round 52 sub-switch routeWeightPerBlock, absent in rounds 48 to 51: a whole-street route count (the volunteer count's four route stations) whose membership is simulated in the period weighs its own weight (routeWeight) times the number of block stations of the same count on the route's links that are fitted with a target in that period and view; with static membership (pass 0, midday, a route without a simulated trip) its weight stays routeWeight. The traversal count is one observation about the whole path and competes in the multiplicative update with one station per block it spans (ASSUMPTION, no reference).

throughTargets._measuredStationsNote: Calibration round 42: fitted volunteer-count blocks inside the study area where the fit's static routes met the count and the simulator did not (class b of the round's diagnosis), PM 14 blocks and AM 5, take their membership from simulated trips: each pair's share of trips on the block over twenty PM (ten AM) seed runs, pooled for PM over the round-40 demand and the round's S2 demand, with the static share as a prior worth priorTrips trips (ASSUMPTION). A block has a simulated membership only in the periods whose file holds its pairs. The training view takes the pairs from runs of the cross-validation demands (measuredStationsTraining), so no run of a demand fitted to held-out counts informs the out-of-sample score. Through targets: membership pooled over the same forty PM runs.
throughTargets._note: Rockridge has whole-street traversal counts. A through-trip fit on any corridor block requires its own measured unique trips with both ends outside the study area (observedCorridorThroughVehPerHour). Link, movement and corridor stations use static assignment unless detector counts come from matching source data, simulator and demand view.

assumedMovementFlows._note: ASSUMPTION (project lead decisions of 2026-11-14, calibration rounds 20 and 21): a counted turning movement the trip table cannot reach gets flows that must make it, so the modeled movement matches the count. Each movement is read from the volunteer count (`count` names the junction, the approach and the exit as the count file words them; its station targets give the volume per period, so midday takes the PM count times the period ratio as every other count does). The flows carry a `via` movement, which the simulator honors by routing the trip to the movement's approach link, through the movement, and on to its destination (re-routing keeps the movement until it is made), and the fit pins their volume. Round 21: the cars that make a movement are described by `intents`, each a named origin group, destination group and volume (a `share` of the movement's counted volume, or `vehPerHour` in the PM peak, scaled with the count in other periods). The groups are the approach groups of the area config (`approachGroups`; `study-area` is the study area's own nodes). The candidates of an intent are the flows of the seed table between its groups whose route through the movement costs at most `maxDetour` times their best route at free flow (the simulator router's cost) and does not loop; the intent's volume is split over them in proportion to their seed volume. The plain flow of each pair then gives up the trips its assumed flow carries (never more than 80% of it), and the fit rescales it to the counts, so total trips between the groups are not counted twice at the start of the fit. Round 26: plain flows of other pairs whose best route makes the same turn (within `naturalDetour` of their best route) give up volume until the turn carries no more than its count, because the fit cannot take a flow below 0.1 of its seed volume and the turn was overshot. A movement counted below the count fit's minimum (`volunteerCount.minMovementVeh`) has no station and no trips in that period; the Assumptions data shows its count. Intents of one movement add up to at most its counted volume, and their shares apply to the turning cars of the count (a car going straight on has no movement station). Every volume that is not a count is an ASSUMPTION; the data say which. Nothing here is area specific in code.

movements.wholeStreetNote: ASSUMPTION (round 25): the through intents (SR-24 off-ramp and south-side traffic) take only seed flows whose route to this movement drives Colby St northbound from its first link. The count has 102 cars driving the whole street and the model had 80: the through flows reached the Alcatraz Ave turn from 63rd St and the other side streets, which the count says the whole-street cars do not (182 entered at the south end).
movements.maxDetourNote: ASSUMPTION: as for the Colby St left turn (round 20): drivers perceive route costs with an error (8% per link until round 31, probit dispersion since), so a pair within 30% of its best route is one whose drivers could pick either.

The count has 102 cars driving the whole street and the model had 80: the through flows reached the Alcatraz Ave turn from 63rd St and the other side streets, which the count says the whole-street cars do not (182 entered at the south end).

assumedMovementFlows.naturalDetourNote: ASSUMPTION (round 26): a plain flow whose best route through a movement costs at most this multiple of its best route makes that turn naturally. Drivers perceive route costs with an error (8% per link until round 31, probit dispersion since), so a route within 5% of the best is one drivers take part of the time.
assumedMovementFlows.alternativesNote: ASSUMPTION (via-detour-fallback, round 26): the builder writes `via.maxDetour` (each movement's `maxDetour`) on every assumed flow and, for a through flow (no end in the study area), `via.alternatives`: the other movements that have an intent whose origin and destination groups contain the flow's groups. The simulator makes the movement only while the route through it costs at most `maxDetour` times the plain route in the current network and passes no node twice, else it takes the cheapest alternative that passes, else the plain route. A flow with an end in the study area (a resident's trip) has no alternatives and falls back to its plain route, so a scenario does not move a Colby St resident's trip to Hillegass Ave. Nothing here is area specific in code.

volunteerCount._note: DATA: resident volunteer turning-movement count, Tuesday 2025-02-25, 8-9 AM and 5-6 PM (data/calibration/README.md). Blocks are directed-link volume constraints; turning movements and whole-street routes constrain the share of assigned routes. One day, one hour: weights and tolerances below are ASSUMPTIONS. Midday has no count.

otherThrough._note: ASSUMPTION (round 19): entries of streets with no whole-street count take the through share of the counted whole streets (268 of 593 entering cars in the PM peak, 45%; Martin Street in the AM peak shows 48%), so the count-implied study-area trip ends (804 destinations and 817 origins in the PM peak, against 927 and 940 when only the counted streets were through) are not overstated. The rate-sheet check [PBC-TripRates2022]: 0.94 PM peak trips per detached dwelling, so these 1,621 ends need about 1,700 dwellings, against 1,368 resident workers in the study area (dwellings are not in the data held; 2020 census block housing units need an API key).

intersectionCounts._note: DATA: peak-hour turning-movement counts from published environmental impact reports (file below; data/demand/README.md, seventeenth round). Each leg gives a volume entering and leaving on its links (weight as a turning-movement leg), left and right turns of at least minMovementVeh are movement constraints (movementWeight, they restate part of the legs), and a counted ramp leg replaces the ramp ADT x K station (rampWeight). ASSUMPTION: no growth from the count year; midday takes the PM count times the ratio of the period volume factors at middayWeightFactor of the weight; a ramp without a count in a period keeps its ADT-based target scaled by the count ratio of the PM peak.
